# What should you reorder this week, and what is just cash on a shelf?

> Free reorder planner for Shopify and other small online stores: load an orders export and a stock export and see each SKU's reorder point, how many to order, revenue at risk from stock-outs and cash tied up in overstock. Runs in your browser, files are never uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Results are estimates from the files supplied, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## What it does

- Reads Shopify's Orders export, or any CSV with a date, a SKU (or product name) and a quantity, including invoice-style exports (`StockCode`, `Description`, `InvoiceDate`). Large exports (a million lines) are fine.
- Reorder point = velocity x lead time + safety stock. Safety stock is chosen per SKU: lumpy or intermittent sellers (selling on fewer than about 3 days in 4) take the service-level quantile of their own demand over every lead-time-long run in the file; steady sellers use z x weekly standard deviation scaled to the lead time.
- Measured on a real store (UCI Online Retail II, 1,067,371 order lines, 3,078 SKUs, a year held out, 14-day lead time, 95% setting): the per-SKU rule kept the shelf stocked through 80.7% of lead times vs 77.5% for the weekly-only rule, with 3.5% less stock. Neither reaches the promised 95% on that lumpy, wholesale-heavy store.
